A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Nearly-Optimal Bandit Learning in Stackelberg Games with Side Information. All 17 pages, including figures, equations, and Appendices A–B, support comparison; the four appendix pages are identical.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic Stackelberg-game simulations in Section 3.5 and Appendix A.1, with cumulative utility and regret results in Figures 1–2.

after.justification: v3 retains the original simulations and their reported outcomes in Section 3.5, Appendix A.1, and Figures 1–2.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3, the utility-space reduction, OFUL and logdet-FTRL instantiations, and the unknown-utility extension are unchanged. The added natural-language example introduces no algorithmic component or input-processing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic Stackelberg games with context-dependent and context-independent follower utilities. Natural-language reports and briefings are newly mentioned as motivating examples, but no such data or task is evaluated.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains the random baseline and optimal-policy reference. Figure 2a retains the random baseline and Harris et al. (2024) Algorithm 3, called Barycentric Explore-Then-Commit; Figure 2b retains the random baseline. The new citations are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Figures 1–2 retain their respective 200- and 2,000-round horizons, follower counts, action counts, context dimensions, and utility/regret metrics. Stochastic data generation and the reported tuning of the Harris baseline are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The comparisons in Section 3.5 and Appendix A.1 are unchanged. Neither version contains additional ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness analyses, or empirical case studies absent from the other.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging over 10 runs and display identical shaded bands in Figures 1–2. There are no changes to run-count disclosures, seed information, uncertainty definitions, or statistical testing.

E6.justification: All four plot panels in Figures 1–2 are identical. Both versions retain the same utility and regret trajectories and the finding that Algorithm 1-OFUL outperforms the random baseline and Barycentric Explore-Then-Commit where applicable.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, regret guarantees, runtime arguments, and proofs are unchanged. Definition 2.1 and several other passages cross different page boundaries in v3, but their mathematical content is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same near-optimal regret claim, utility-space reduction, unknown-utility extension, auction and persuasion applications, and empirical superiority claim. The added contextual example does not redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: The introduction newly discusses natural-language embeddings of threat reports, incident descriptions, and intelligence briefings as side information affecting strategic decisions. This modestly expands the applicability discussion; existing result interpretations and limitations concerning runtime and unknown utilities remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Experimental setup disclosures and the baseline hyperparameter-tuning note are unchanged. No implementation details, reproducibility instructions, hardware information, or code/data access information are added or revised.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds Balcan et al. (2026), Learning in Structured Stackelberg Games, distinguishing its setting where side information predicts follower type. It also adds Harris et al. (2023a), Meta-learning in Games, and Harris et al. (2023b), Strategic Apple Tasting. Existing positioning is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v3 adds a short introductory example and limited related-work text, changes the acknowledgment heading spelling, and expands MB to Martino Bernasconi in the funding statement. The section organization and technical exposition remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Added prose causes local text and reference reflow: Section 3.5 now continues onto page 8, and the conclusion starts on page 10. Figures, captions, algorithm displays, and appendix layouts retain their designs and content.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves research positioning by explicitly distinguishing the closely related predictive-side-information setting of Balcan et al. (2026) and adding relevant meta-learning and strategic-classification references. The natural-language example also clarifies possible contextual inputs. These are limited gains in motivation and contextualization; the methods, proofs, empirical evidence, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
